title: What Mentoring My Younger Cousin Taught Me About Family Obligation
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] When my aunt asked if I'd look after my cousin Rian while he studied in this city, I agreed mostly out of obligation, without giving much thought to what it would actually require.
Narrator: I imagined occasional dinners and a bit of advice, not the near-weekly crises that followed: failed exams, a landlord dispute, a friendship that ended badly.
Narrator: [carefully] There were nights I resented the responsibility, wondering why I'd essentially been assigned to raise a nineteen-year-old I barely knew before he arrived.
Narrator: Slowly, though, something shifted. Rian began calling not because he was in crisis, but simply to talk, which felt like an entirely different kind of trust being extended.
Narrator: [reflective] I started noticing how much of what I told him, I had never actually said to my own younger self, about failure, about patience, about not measuring worth by grades alone.
Narrator: In a strange way, mentoring him forced me to examine choices I had made years earlier, ones I'd never fully questioned until I had to justify them to someone else.
Narrator: [honestly] When he failed a course last semester, I caught myself about to deliver exactly the lecture my own father once gave me, word for word, and I stopped myself halfway through.
Narrator: Instead, I told him what I'd actually needed to hear back then, that failure wasn't a referendum on his worth, just an uncomfortable but temporary setback.
Narrator: [gently] He cried, a little, and admitted he'd been terrified to tell anyone, assuming disappointment was the only response available to him.
Narrator: That conversation taught me more about family than any obligation ever had: that being trusted with someone's failure is a far greater responsibility than merely supervising their success.
Narrator: [calmly] Rian graduates next year, and I doubt he'll ever fully know how much this arrangement, which I once viewed as an imposition, ended up reshaping how I see my own family duties.
Narrator: What began as a favor to my aunt became, unexpectedly, one of the relationships I value most.
Narrator: [encouraging] I used to think mentoring meant having answers; now I think it mostly means being willing to stay present while someone else finds theirs.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator originally agree to look after Rian?
options: She wanted a roommate
She agreed mostly out of obligation, without much thought about what it would require
Rian offered to pay her
She had always wanted to mentor someone
quiz.explanation: She agreed mostly out of obligation, without giving much thought to what it would actually require.

quiz.question: What shift did the narrator notice in Rian's calls over time?
options: He stopped calling entirely
He only called to ask for money
He began calling simply to talk, not only when in crisis
He started calling his mother instead
quiz.explanation: Rian began calling not because he was in crisis, but simply to talk, which felt like a different kind of trust.

quiz.question: What did the narrator catch herself about to do when Rian failed a course?
options: Deliver the exact same lecture her own father once gave her
Ignore the situation completely
Call his mother immediately
Tell him to drop out of school
quiz.explanation: She caught herself about to deliver exactly the lecture her own father once gave her, word for word, and stopped halfway through.

quiz.question: What did the narrator tell Rian instead of that lecture?
options: That he should switch universities
That he needed to try harder next time
That grades don't matter at all
That failure wasn't a referendum on his worth, just a temporary setback
quiz.explanation: She told him failure wasn't a referendum on his worth, just an uncomfortable but temporary setback.

quiz.question: What does the narrator conclude mentoring mostly means?
options: Always having the right answers
Supervising someone's every decision
Being willing to stay present while someone else finds their own answers
Avoiding difficult conversations
quiz.explanation: She concludes mentoring mostly means being willing to stay present while someone else finds theirs, rather than having answers.

quiz.question: Why did mentoring Rian initially feel heavier than expected?
options: Weekly crises demanded far more than occasional dinners and advice.
This topic matters a lot to me
No; it complicated the result without completely reversing it.
The treasurer supplied the complete conversation with the volunteer's permission.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Weekly crises demanded far more than occasional dinners and advice.

quiz.question: What change showed that Rian's relationship with the narrator was deepening?
options: That's an easy assumption to make, especially if it's how you were raised to host gatherings yourself
A smaller play space could be combined with trees and benches.
It replaced a public takedown demand with a documented repair process.
He began calling simply to talk rather than only during crises.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He began calling simply to talk rather than only during crises.

quiz.question: Why did the narrator stop repeating his father's old lecture?
options: I'd say it's less about elaborate planning and more about paying attention
He recognised that Rian needed reassurance rather than inherited criticism.
A fair process examines access, information, and affected interests.
The chair reviewed conduct, recorded the repair, and addressed the real harm.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: He recognised that Rian needed reassurance rather than inherited criticism.

quiz.question: What did Rian's fear of sharing failure teach the narrator?
options: Just that hospitality isn't really about the food or the decorations
Being trusted with failure carries greater responsibility than praising success.
Ask who could respond, what they knew, and who bears the effects.
Checking evidence can confirm harm instead of dismissing it.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Being trusted with failure carries greater responsibility than praising success.

quiz.question: How has the narrator's definition of mentoring changed?
options: I hope it encourages someone else to think a little differently about their next gathering
It can collect opinions efficiently from people able to participate.
It means staying present while another person discovers their own answers.
Establish authenticity, context, and consent before spreading or judging it.
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: It means staying present while another person discovers their own answers.
